question.text: A projectile A is thrown at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal from point P. At the same time, another projectile $\mathrm{B}$ is thrown with velocity $\mathrm{v}_{2}$ upwards from the point $Q$ vertically below the highest point. For $\mathrm{B}$ to collide with $\mathrm{A}, \frac{\mathrm{v}_{2}}{\mathrm{v}_{1}}$ should be

solution.text:
This happen when vertical velocity of both are same.

$\therefore v_{2}=v_{1} \sin 30^{\circ} \text { or } \frac{v_{2}}{v_{1}}=\frac{1}{2}$
